Rendering your GIF

Processing on your device…

A little smaller. A lot more control.

Open a GIF, combine your edits across the tools, then Render GIF. Switch between Original and Output to inspect the result. Download exports the selected render; editing settings does not change a render until you render again.

A good compression workflow

  1. Start with Quality: no lossy compression, with source palettes preserved.
  2. Try Balanced, then increase lossiness gradually. Inspect fine text, gradients, and motion.
  3. Reduce dimensions to the size you actually need. Try 128 colors with ordered dithering if gradients shimmer.
  4. Keep every second frame with Preserve duration for a smaller file with the same playback length.
  5. Use the optional target size to try progressively stronger compression. It is a best-effort search, not a size guarantee.

What each control does

Lossiness: 0 preserves palette pixels during compression; larger values allow more visible artifacts. This is an engine setting, not a quality percentage. Dithering: simulates missing colors; can improve gradients but increase size. Optimization: stores only changing regions or pixels. Full frames: useful if another app displays optimized GIFs incorrectly.

Timing uses one-based frame numbers. Frame removal deletes those frames and their duration. Frame reduction can merge the skipped durations into retained frames. GIF delays are rounded to 10 ms, with a 20 ms minimum when timing changes; source 0/10 ms delays are interpreted as 100 ms to match common browser behavior. Repeat counts mean additional plays. Bounce excludes repeated end frames.

Live edits show color, text, geometry, frame order, and timing before compression. GIF palette quantization and compression artifacts appear only in a rendered result. Preview resize filters approximate the export resamplers. In comparison views both animations share an elapsed-time playhead and keep their own timing; the preview loops for comparison even when export is set to play once. Edits always start from the original file, so experiments do not stack quality loss. Resize and crop apply before text and effects. Text and effects require a new 256-color palette and may change colors, even at lossiness 0. Dithering then applies to any further palette reduction. Resize dimensions refer to the cropped, rotated image. Preview backgrounds do not change exported transparency; use the matte control to flatten it.

Size estimates and frame editing

Small animations are fully calculated in the background with the actual export engine. For larger animations, short frame blocks are sampled and encoded using your settings, then extrapolated to a broad estimated range. Content and frame optimization can make the final file differ. Target-size search runs only when you render. Estimates do not create a saved result. Downloads always use the selected rendered GIF.

The visual Frames view shows the output sequence. Adjust a delay, move a frame, or delete selected frames to switch to a custom sequence; those edits replace automatic trim/reduction/reverse settings. Global speed still applies. Use Original order to reset the sequence. Thumbnails show source frames; the live preview includes your image edits.

Presets, replacement files and history

Presets saves named settings in this browser. Apply a preset, adjust any tool, then choose Update from current. You can rename or delete presets, undo the last preset change, and export/import a JSON backup. By default presets exclude exact frame edits; enable that option to include source-frame order, individual delays, removals and trim. No image data is stored.

Replacing a GIF keeps compatible compression, dimensions, timing, effects and captions. Crop and trim ranges are fitted to the new source; exact frame reorder, removals and individual delays are cleared. Output dimensions respect the new aspect ratio when locked. Invalid timing or oversized outputs are adjusted and reported. Settings history restarts for each source.

Undo and Redo work for settings, preset application, reset and frame edits. Use Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y outside text fields, or the visible buttons. Reset all restores editor defaults without deleting saved presets or renders. Presets use browser storage, which may depend on the HTML file’s name and location. Export a backup before moving the file or switching browsers. If storage is unavailable, the editor clearly marks presets as session-only.

Local by design

This HTML contains its processing code and WebAssembly. It makes no network requests, uploads no files, and stores no image data between sessions. Named presets and your theme are stored locally when browser storage is available. You can disconnect from the internet after downloading it. Open it in a current desktop Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari browser. Browser and workplace policy may restrict local scripts or downloads.

The editor supports GIF input/output and individual PNG frame export. It does not include Ezgif’s video converters, GIF creation from multiple images, animated WebP/APNG export, overlays, or AI tools. Local safeguards: 50 MB input, 4,096 px maximum dimension, 1,500 frames, and 180 million canvas pixels across frames. Very large animations may still exceed available browser memory.

Research & open-source credits

Inspired by the workflow described in Ezgif’s optimization guide, resizer, and timing tool. Independent tool; no affiliation with Ezgif.
